content.title: About
content.content: Soft NFS breadsticks are tender, lightly toasted sticks made from wheat flour following a classic recipe. They have a soft texture, a subtle buttery aroma, and a mildly sweet flavor, making them perfect for snacking or as a side to meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Breadsticks originated in Italy as “grissini,” but the soft version became popular in the United States in the 1970s.
NFS (Not For Sale) is an internal company code indicating the product is intended for internal café use only.
Soft sticks are often served with dips such as marinara, cheese sauce, or hummus.
Unlike crunchy sticks, soft ones retain moisture longer, allowing them to be used in hot dishes like casseroles.
Traditionally they are made without preservatives, relying on fresh ingredients.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Breadsticks provide a quick source of energy thanks to the carbohydrates they contain.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: The wheat flour used supplies B1, B2, and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Soft sticks usually contain little fat, especially when prepared without added butter.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The soft texture makes them gentle on the stomach, suitable for children and seniors.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain flour is used, the fiber content increases, aiding digestion.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The product contains gluten and may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of the simple carbs, breadsticks can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions are heavily salted; those monitoring sodium should choose unsalted options.

items.title: Short shelf life
items.content: The soft texture makes the product more prone to spoilage; store in a dry cool place and consume within a few days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Breadsticks can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, dipped in sauces, added to salads, used as a base for canapés, or served alongside soups and stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, refrigerate; they will stay soft for up to a week.
